cultural.vision_reason: A carved stone maul head with a zoomorphic (salmon/whale) crest and grooves for hafting—this is a characteristic Northwest Coast stone hammer/maul tool type, consistent with Tsimshian material culture.

physical.title: hammer
physical.summary: Maul [hammer] head of a light grey igneous rock, with a flat work surface, oval cross section, and crest probably in the form of a salmon head. Parallel to the work surface round the maul is a decorative groove, followed by a deeper groove, for the binding to attach the handle. This would fitted along the bottom of the head. The head is carved with deep circular eyes, delineated with two incised lines and a deep broad groove, a long straight groove mouth, on top of the head is lightly incised carved head, more suggestive of a whale's blowhole than a salmon. The rock has a natural fault line it, and a large piece is moving close to groove for attachment.
